Before we begin, I want to share an experience that shaped the direction of my career. I never imagined that a mistake while enrolling in my courses would end up sparking my interest in one of the most important areas of software development.

During my second semester of Systems Engineering, I accidentally ended up in an elective course called **Software Testing and Quality**. What seemed like a simple mistake turned into one of the best experiences of my academic journey and helped me discover that software quality is just as important as software development.

Now, I invite you to discover what a QA Automation Engineer really does and why this role is much more important than many people imagine.
en.excerpt:
When I started researching the different areas of systems engineering, I discovered that many people think a QA Automation Engineer only focuses on finding bugs. However, as I learned more about this profession, I understood that their work goes much further.

My first experience with the world of software testing was during my second semester of Systems Engineering. When I was enrolling in my courses, due to an error in the university platform, I ended up registered in an elective course called Software Testing and Quality. When I arrived in the classroom, I was surprised to see that most of the students were in the final semesters of the degree.

Although at first I thought it would be a very big challenge for me, I decided to take advantage of the opportunity. As the classes went by, I discovered an area that completely caught my interest. I understood that developing software is only one part of the process, and that ensuring its quality is just as important. That experience changed the way I see software development and sparked my interest in quality assurance and test automation.
highlights: Software quality is just as important as the development of new features.
A QA Automation Engineer does not only find bugs; they help prevent them from the beginning of the project.
Test automation allows teams to develop more reliable, efficient, and scalable software.
A good QA professional combines technical skills, analytical thinking, and teamwork.
Artificial Intelligence is transforming QA, but human judgment remains essential.
Quality assurance is an investment that improves the user experience and reduces costs.
The QA Automation Engineer has become one of the roles with the greatest growth potential in the software industry.
Understanding the value of testing means understanding how quality software is built.
en.introduction:
Every time we use an application to send a message, make a purchase, or check our banking information, we expect everything to work correctly on the first try. However, behind that experience, there is a process of planning, testing, and validation that seeks to ensure that the software is reliable before it reaches users.

In this process, the QA Automation Engineer plays a fundamental role. Their work is not only about finding bugs, but also about designing testing strategies, automating repetitive processes, and collaborating with the development team to deliver higher-quality products.

Throughout this article, we will explore what this profession really involves, its main responsibilities, the tools it uses, and why it has become one of the most in-demand roles in the software industry.
paragraphs:
# What Is a QA Automation Engineer?

A QA Automation Engineer is the professional responsible for ensuring that software works correctly before it reaches users. To achieve this, they design testing strategies, create automated tests, and verify that features meet the established requirements.

Although many people think this role is only about finding bugs, the reality is very different. Their work begins even before a feature is developed, by participating in the understanding of requirements, identifying possible risks, and proposing ways to validate that the product works as expected.

# What Is Their Role Within a Development Team?

A QA Automation Engineer works collaboratively with developers, analysts, designers, and project leaders. Their goal is not to point out who made a mistake, but to help the team deliver a higher-quality product.

Generally, their work includes activities such as:

- Analyzing the requirements of a new feature.
- Designing test cases for different scenarios.
- Automating repetitive tests using specialized tools.
- Running tests before each new release.
- Reporting bugs with clear and detailed information.
- Validating that issues have been fixed.
- Contributing to the continuous improvement of the development process.

Thanks to this work, bugs can be detected before they affect end users, reducing costs and improving software reliability.

# Tools Used by a QA Automation Engineer

Test automation requires the use of different tools that help speed up the process and increase test coverage.

Some of the most commonly used tools are:

-**Playwright**, for automating tests in modern web applications.
-**Selenium**, one of the most well-known tools for browser automation.
-**Postman**, for testing and validating APIs.
-**Git**, for version control and collaborative work.
-**SQL**, for querying and verifying information stored in databases.
-**Jira**, for managing tasks, issues, and bug reports.
-**Docker** and **CI/CD** tools, which allow tests to run automatically during the integration and deployment process.

Knowing these technologies allows a QA Automation Engineer to actively participate throughout the entire software development life cycle.

# Required Skills

Beyond technical knowledge, a good QA professional needs to develop skills that allow them to understand the product and anticipate possible problems.

Among the most important skills, I consider the following:

- Analytical thinking.
- Attention to detail.
- Problem-solving skills.
- Effective communication with the team.
- Organization and planning.
- Curiosity to learn new tools and technologies.

On the technical side, it is recommended to have a foundation in programming, test automation, databases, version control, and agile methodologies.

# Will Artificial Intelligence Replace QA Professionals?

In my opinion, Artificial Intelligence will not replace the work of a QA Automation Engineer, but it will transform the way they work. Today, there are already tools capable of generating test cases, writing part of the automation code, or detecting possible errors. However, people are still needed to understand the business, interpret the results, and make decisions about product quality.

AI should be understood as a tool that enhances the work of QA professionals, allowing them to spend more time on analysis and less time on repetitive tasks.

# Conclusion

My first experience with the world of QA happened by chance, but over time I discovered a profession that combines analysis, programming, problem-solving, and continuous improvement. Today, I understand that a QA Automation Engineer does not only look for bugs: they help build more reliable products and contribute to ensuring that technology reaches people with the quality they expect.

If you are studying Systems Engineering or are interested in software development, I invite you to explore this area. Maybe, just like it happened to me, you will discover a profession that completely changes the way you see how good software is built.
en.phrase: “Quality doesn’t happen by accident; it is built through testing.”
en.title: What does a QA Automation Engineer really do?

paragraphs:
# ¿Qué es un QA Automation Engineer?

Un QA Automation Engineer es el profesional encargado de garantizar que un software funcione correctamente antes de llegar a los usuarios. Para lograrlo, diseña estrategias de prueba, crea pruebas automatizadas y verifica que las funcionalidades cumplan con los requisitos establecidos.

Aunque muchas personas piensan que este rol consiste únicamente en encontrar errores, la realidad es muy diferente. Su trabajo comienza incluso antes de que una funcionalidad sea desarrollada, participando en la comprensión de los requisitos, identificando posibles riesgos y proponiendo formas de validar que el producto funcione como se espera.

# ¿Cuál es su función dentro de un equipo de desarrollo?

El QA Automation Engineer trabaja de manera colaborativa con desarrolladores, analistas, diseñadores y líderes de proyecto. Su objetivo no es señalar quién cometió un error, sino contribuir a que el equipo entregue un producto de mayor calidad.

Generalmente, su trabajo incluye actividades como:

- Analizar los requisitos de una nueva funcionalidad.
- Diseñar casos de prueba para diferentes escenarios.
- Automatizar pruebas repetitivas utilizando herramientas especializadas.
- Ejecutar pruebas antes de cada nueva versión.
- Reportar errores encontrados con información clara y detallada.
- Validar que los problemas hayan sido corregidos.
- Contribuir a mejorar continuamente el proceso de desarrollo.

Gracias a este trabajo, los errores pueden detectarse antes de que afecten a los usuarios finales, reduciendo costos y mejorando la confiabilidad del software.

# Herramientas que utiliza un QA Automation Engineer

La automatización de pruebas requiere apoyarse en diferentes herramientas que permiten agilizar el proceso y aumentar la cobertura de las pruebas.

Algunas de las más utilizadas son:

- **Playwright**, para automatizar pruebas en aplicaciones web modernas.
- **Selenium**, una de las herramientas más conocidas para automatización de navegadores.
- **Postman**, para probar y validar APIs.
- **Git**, para el control de versiones y el trabajo colaborativo.
- **SQL**, para consultar y verificar la información almacenada en bases de datos.
- **Jira**, para gestionar tareas, incidencias y reportes de errores.
- **Docker** y herramientas de **CI/CD**, que permiten ejecutar pruebas automáticamente durante el proceso de integración y despliegue.

Conocer estas tecnologías permite al QA Automation Engineer participar activamente en todo el ciclo de desarrollo del software.

# Habilidades necesarias

Más allá del conocimiento técnico, un buen profesional de QA necesita desarrollar habilidades que le permitan comprender el producto y anticiparse a posibles problemas.

Entre las más importantes considero que se encuentran:

- Pensamiento analítico.
- Atención al detalle.
- Capacidad para resolver problemas.
- Comunicación efectiva con el equipo.
- Organización y planificación.
- Curiosidad por aprender nuevas herramientas y tecnologías.

En el aspecto técnico, es recomendable tener bases de programación, automatización de pruebas, bases de datos, control de versiones y metodologías ágiles.

# ¿La Inteligencia Artificial reemplazará a los QA?

En mi opinión, la Inteligencia Artificial no reemplazará el trabajo de un QA Automation Engineer, pero sí transformará la manera en que trabaja. Hoy en día ya existen herramientas capaces de generar casos de prueba, escribir parte del código de automatización o detectar posibles errores. Sin embargo, siguen siendo necesarias personas que comprendan el negocio, interpreten los resultados y tomen decisiones sobre la calidad del producto.

La IA debe entenderse como una herramienta que potencia el trabajo del QA, permitiéndole dedicar más tiempo al análisis y menos a las tareas repetitivas.

# Conclusión

Mi primer acercamiento al mundo del QA ocurrió por casualidad, pero con el tiempo descubrí una profesión que combina análisis, programación, resolución de problemas y mejora continua. Hoy entiendo que un QA Automation Engineer no solo busca errores: ayuda a construir productos más confiables y contribuye a que la tecnología llegue a las personas con la calidad que esperan.

Si estás estudiando Ingeniería de Sistemas o te interesa el desarrollo de software, te invito a explorar esta área. Tal vez, como me ocurrió a mí, descubras una profesión que cambie por completo tu forma de ver cómo se construye un buen software.

en.excerpt:
When talking about software testing, it is common to hear the terms Manual QA and QA Automation, and even to think that both perform exactly the same work or that one will eventually replace the other. However, the reality is very different. Although both share the same goal of ensuring software quality, each one provides a different approach, set of tools, and responsibilities within the development process.

In this article, we will explore the main differences between Manual QA and QA Automation, the skills each profile requires, their advantages, the scenarios where they are most effective, and how both complement each other to build more reliable applications. If you are thinking about starting a career in the world of QA or simply want to better understand these two areas, this guide will help you understand which one may best fit your interests and professional goals.
highlights: Manual QA and QA Automation do not compete; they complement each other to ensure software quality.
Manual testing is essential for exploring, analyzing, and understanding the behavior of an application.
Automation allows repetitive tests to be executed in a faster, more consistent, and scalable way.
Choosing between Manual QA and QA Automation depends on the context, the needs of the project, and the goals of the team.
Programming expands the possibilities of a QA professional, but analytical thinking remains just as important.

en.introduction:
Software quality has become one of the most important factors for the success of any application. Users expect fast, reliable, and error-free systems, which has led software testing to play a fundamental role within the development process.

In this context, two profiles often create confusion: Manual QA and QA Automation. Although both share the same goal of ensuring software quality, their responsibilities, tools, and ways of working are different. While one focuses on exploration, analysis, and manual validation of features, the other uses programming and automation to run tests in a faster, more efficient, and repeatable way.

Understanding the differences between these two approaches not only helps us understand how quality software is built, but also helps identify which one may better fit the interests and professional goals of those who want to start a career in the world of quality assurance.
paragraphs:
# What Is Manual QA?

Manual QA is the professional responsible for verifying that an application works correctly by executing tests performed by a person, without relying on scripts or automation tools. Their work consists of exploring the system, validating that each feature meets the requirements, and detecting possible errors before the software reaches users.

This type of testing is especially useful during the early stages of development, when features change frequently or when it is necessary to evaluate aspects that require human judgment, such as user experience, ease of use, or the general behavior of an application.

Among the main activities of a Manual QA are:

- Designing and executing test cases.
- Identifying and documenting bugs.
- Performing exploratory testing.
- Validating new features.
- Verifying fixes before a new release.

Although many tests are performed manually, this role requires analytical skills, attention to detail, and a deep understanding of how the product works.

# What Is QA Automation?

A QA Automation Engineer has the same goal as a Manual QA: to ensure software quality. The difference is that they use programming and specialized tools to automate tests that would normally need to be executed repeatedly.

Instead of manually performing the same validations in each new release, they develop scripts capable of running them automatically, reducing time, increasing test coverage, and decreasing the possibility of human error.

Among their main responsibilities are:

- Automating functional tests.
- Creating and maintaining test scripts.
- Running tests automatically within continuous integration processes (CI/CD).
- Validating APIs and databases.
- Collaborating with developers to improve software quality.

To perform this role, it is recommended to have knowledge of programming, version control, databases, and automation tools such as Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress.

# Main Differences Between Manual QA and QA Automation

Although both profiles pursue the same goal, there are important differences in the way they perform their work.

| Field               | Manual QA        | QA Automation  |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | -------------- |
| Test execution      | Manual           | Automated      |
| Programming         | Not essential    | Necessary      |
| Speed               | Lower            | Higher         |
| Repetitive tests    | Less efficient   | Very efficient |
| Exploratory testing | Excellent option | Limited        |
| Test coverage       | Lower            | Higher         |
| Initial investment  | Low              | Higher         |
| Scalability         | Limited          | Very high      |

Rather than competing with each other, both approaches complement one another. While Manual QA contributes analysis, exploration, and human judgment, QA Automation allows large volumes of tests to be executed quickly, repeatedly, and consistently.

# Conclusion

Understanding the differences between Manual QA and QA Automation allows us to value the role that both play within software development. Although they use different approaches, they both share the same goal: ensuring that applications reach users with the highest possible quality.

Manual testing remains essential for exploring new features, identifying unexpected behaviors, and providing the human judgment that no tool can completely replace. On the other hand, automation allows tests to be executed quickly, consistently, and scalably, becoming a fundamental ally for projects that are constantly evolving.

Rather than choosing which one is better, the important thing is to understand when to use each approach and how both complement each other to build more reliable software. If you are thinking about starting a career in the world of QA, knowing these differences will be the first step in deciding the path that best fits your interests and professional goals.
en.phrase: "Quality begins with manual testing and evolves with automation."
en.title: Manual QA vs QA Automation: What’s the Difference?

La calidad del software se ha convertido en uno de los factores más importantes para el éxito de cualquier aplicación. Los usuarios esperan sistemas rápidos, confiables y libres de errores, lo que ha llevado a que las pruebas de software desempeñen un papel fundamental dentro del proceso de desarrollo.

En este contexto surgen dos perfiles que suelen generar confusión: QA Manual y QA Automation. Aunque ambos comparten el mismo objetivo de garantizar la calidad del software, sus responsabilidades, herramientas y forma de trabajar son diferentes. Mientras uno se enfoca en la exploración, el análisis y la validación manual de las funcionalidades, el otro utiliza la programación y la automatización para ejecutar pruebas de manera más rápida, eficiente y repetible.

Comprender las diferencias entre estos dos enfoques no solo ayuda a entender cómo se construye un software de calidad, sino también a identificar cuál puede adaptarse mejor a los intereses y objetivos profesionales de quienes desean iniciar una carrera en el mundo del aseguramiento de la calidad.
paragraphs:
# ¿Qué es QA Manual?

El QA Manual es el profesional encargado de verificar que una aplicación funcione correctamente mediante la ejecución de pruebas realizadas por una persona, sin depender de scripts o herramientas de automatización. Su trabajo consiste en explorar el sistema, validar que cada funcionalidad cumpla con los requisitos y detectar posibles errores antes de que el software llegue a los usuarios.

Este tipo de pruebas resulta especialmente útil durante las primeras etapas del desarrollo, cuando las funcionalidades cambian con frecuencia o cuando es necesario evaluar aspectos que requieren criterio humano, como la experiencia del usuario, la facilidad de uso o el comportamiento general de una aplicación.

Entre las principales actividades de un QA Manual se encuentran:

- Diseñar y ejecutar casos de prueba.
- Identificar y documentar errores.
- Realizar pruebas exploratorias.
- Validar nuevas funcionalidades.
- Verificar correcciones antes de una nueva versión.

Aunque muchas pruebas se realizan manualmente, este rol requiere capacidad de análisis, atención al detalle y una comprensión profunda del funcionamiento del producto.

# ¿Qué es QA Automation?

El QA Automation Engineer tiene el mismo objetivo que un QA Manual: garantizar la calidad del software. La diferencia es que utiliza programación y herramientas especializadas para automatizar pruebas que normalmente deberían ejecutarse de forma repetitiva.

En lugar de realizar manualmente las mismas validaciones en cada nueva versión, desarrolla scripts capaces de ejecutarlas de manera automática, reduciendo tiempos, aumentando la cobertura de las pruebas y disminuyendo la posibilidad de errores humanos.

Entre sus principales responsabilidades se encuentran:

- Automatizar pruebas funcionales.
- Crear y mantener scripts de prueba.
- Ejecutar pruebas automáticamente dentro de procesos de integración continua (CI/CD).
- Validar APIs y bases de datos.
- Colaborar con desarrolladores para mejorar la calidad del software.

Para desempeñar este rol es recomendable tener conocimientos de programación, control de versiones, bases de datos y herramientas de automatización como Playwright, Selenium o Cypress.

# Principales diferencias entre QA Manual y QA Automation

Aunque ambos perfiles persiguen el mismo objetivo, existen diferencias importantes en la forma en que realizan su trabajo.

| Campo | QA Manual | QA Automation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ejecución de pruebas | Manual | Automatizada |
| Programación | No es indispensable | Es necesario |
| Velocidad | Menor | Mayor |
| Pruebas repetitivas | Poco eficientes | Muy eficientes |
| Pruebas Exploratorias | Excelente opción | Limitadas |
| Cobertura de pruebas | Menor | Mayor |
| Inversión inicial | Baja | Más alta |
| Escalabilidad | Limitada | Muy alta |

Más que competir entre sí, ambos enfoques se complementan. Mientras el QA Manual aporta análisis, exploración y criterio humano, el QA Automation permite ejecutar grandes volúmenes de pruebas de forma rápida, repetible y consistente.

# Conclusión

Comprender las diferencias entre QA Manual y QA Automation permite valorar el papel que ambos desempeñan dentro del desarrollo de software. Aunque utilizan enfoques distintos, los dos comparten el mismo objetivo: garantizar que las aplicaciones lleguen a los usuarios con la mayor calidad posible.

Las pruebas manuales siguen siendo indispensables para explorar nuevas funcionalidades, identificar comportamientos inesperados y aportar el criterio humano que ninguna herramienta puede reemplazar por completo. Por su parte, la automatización permite ejecutar pruebas de forma rápida, consistente y escalable, convirtiéndose en un aliado fundamental para proyectos que evolucionan constantemente.

Más que elegir cuál es mejor, lo importante es entender cuándo utilizar cada enfoque y cómo ambos se complementan para construir software más confiable. Si estás pensando en iniciar una carrera en el mundo del QA, conocer estas diferencias será el primer paso para decidir el camino que mejor se adapte a tus intereses y objetivos profesionales.
es.phrase: "La calidad comienza con las pruebas manuales y evoluciona con la automatización."
